settings.eyebrow: Artisan bakery · Stone-milled flour · Wood-fired oven
settings.headline:
Bread that waits
for the dough, not the clock.
settings.copy: The Hearth & Crumb is a small bakery in the Old Market quarter. We slow-ferment every loaf overnight, mill our own heritage grains, and bake on a wood-fired deck that gives each crust a deep, honeyed colour you can't get any other way.

settings.title: On the
settings.intro: A short, honest list that changes with the seasons and the weather — what the oven can carry well, baked in small numbers so nothing sits. Come early for the loaves; they go fast.

items.name: Country Sourdough
items.description: Our signature 24-hour cold-ferment loaf — crackling crust, open crumb, a gentle tang that deepens with toast and age. Stone-milled wheat, water, salt.

items.name: Heritage Rye
items.description: A dense, faintly sweet loaf built on a rye starter we've kept alive since 2018. Sliced thin, it's the backbone of every good lunch.

items.name: Olive & Rosemary Focaccia
items.description: Wet, blistered, and oiled — slow-proofed overnight with kalamata olives and fresh rosemary from the market. Best torn warm.

items.name: Almond Croissant
items.description: Laminated over three days, filled with house frangipane and toasted almond. Shatters when you bite it.

items.name: Cardamom Knot
items.description: A Scandinavian-style morning bun, heavy on fresh-ground cardamom, finished with pearl sugar and a whisper of lemon.

items.name: Honey & Sea Salt Loaf
items.description: A soft, enriched loaf sweetened with local wildflower honey and flecked with sea salt. Toasts like a dream.

settings.title: Slow food,
settings.intro: There's nothing quick about our bread. It's a long, deliberate process built on the idea that flour, water, salt and time — given room — make something worth waking up early for.

features.title: Stone-milled heritage grains
features.text: We mill our own flour from small farms every week, so nothing ever sits long enough to go stale before it becomes dough. Different seasons, slightly different loaves — that's the point.

features.title: A starter older than the shop
features.text: Our rye starter has been fed every day since 2018. It carries the bakery's whole history, and it's why the sourdough has a depth you can't shortcut.

features.title: Cold ferment, never rushed
features.text: Every loaf sleeps in the fridge for 18 to 24 hours before baking. Slow cold fermentation builds flavour and a crust that stays crisp for days.

features.title: A wood-fired deck
features.text: We bake on a traditional wood-fired deck oven that holds its heat for hours. It gives the crust a deep amber colour and a whisper of smoke you can't fake.

features.title: Small batches, on purpose
features.text: We bake only what we expect to sell. Nothing sits under heat lamps, nothing is made to a frozen schedule — when a batch is gone, it's gone until tomorrow.

features.title: Four ingredients, honestly
features.text: Flour, water, salt and time. No improvers, no preservatives, no secrets. If the recipe needs a list of additives, it isn't bread.

settings.title: How a loaf
settings.intro: Each batch follows the same slow rhythm — a schedule set by the dough's readiness, not by the clock on the wall.

steps.title: Mill the grain
steps.text: Heritage wheat and rye are stone-milled on a Sunday morning, the flour sifted and rested before it meets water.

steps.title: Mix & build the dough
steps.text: Flour, water, salt and a portion of the starter are mixed by hand, then folded at intervals through the afternoon.

steps.title: Cold ferment overnight
steps.text: The dough sleeps in the fridge for 18 to 24 hours, developing flavour and a crust that crackles.

steps.title: Shape & score
steps.text: At first light we shape each loaf by hand and score it with a single clean line, then let it rest before the oven.

steps.title: Bake on the wood deck
steps.text: Loaded onto the hot stone, the loaves bake until the crust turns deep amber and the bakery smells like a morning should.

settings.note: The oven holds its heat for hours, so small batches come out all morning — the last loaf is as fresh as the first.

settings.title: Scenes from
settings.intro: A look at the counter at dawn — fresh scores, blistered focaccia, and the wood deck doing its quiet work.

settings.title: The neighbourhood
settings.intro: People build whole mornings around the smell from the oven. Here's what they say once the coffee's poured.

reviews.quote: I've lived three blocks away for a decade, and I still walk past every bakery in town to get here. The country sourdough is the best loaf in the city, full stop.
reviews.author: Ingrid Voss

reviews.quote: The cardamom knots are worth getting up early for. But it's the almond croissant that ruined every other bakery for me. It shatters. It's perfect.
reviews.author: Marcus Bell

reviews.quote: You can taste the difference the moment you break the crust — that open crumb, that long ferment. This is real bread, made properly, and you can tell.
reviews.author: Priya Anand

settings.title: Come by
settings.intro: We're in the Old Market quarter, on the corner of Mill Lane and Baker Street. The door opens at 7am; the oven never stops until the last loaf is out. Come early for the loaves.
